title: This Snake Fakes Its Own Death, and It Always Overacts

scenes.text: This snake dies every time you scare it. Then it gets up.
The eastern hognose snake of North America. Two to three feet long, harmless to people, and the best actor in the animal kingdom.
Act one: it flattens its neck like a cobra, hisses, and strikes. With its mouth closed. It's a head-butt.
If that fails, act two. It thrashes, rolls onto its back, mouth open, tongue hanging out, and releases a foul stink. Dead.
Here's the giveaway. Roll it right side up, and it immediately flips onto its back again. Dead snakes don't do that.
Once you leave, it turns over, looks around, and slides off to hunt toads. It's immune to their poison. The only thing it can't survive is a critic.

description:
The eastern hognose snake fakes its own death when threatened: it flattens its neck like a cobra, hisses and head-butts with its mouth closed, then rolls onto its back with its tongue out, releases a foul musk and plays dead.
The giveaway is that if you roll it right side up, it flips straight back over. It is nonvenomous to people, grows 20 to 33 inches, and eats mostly toads, whose toxins it is immune to.
What is the best animal bluff you have ever seen?
subject: hognose snake
first_comment: It even regurgitates its last meal to sell the act. Which animal do you think is the best actor?
